standard_prerequisites.name: The criterion for a localized site to have enough points
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the hypothesis on the localized sites and the conclusion there.

standard_prerequisites.name: Points of a localized site give points of the site
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the points of the localized sites into points of the ambient site.

core_obligations: Reduction (proof lines 9668-9674): by the companion proposition each localized site has enough points, and its points give points of the ambient site; it therefore suffices to show that a map which becomes an isomorphism on every localized site is an isomorphism.

The verification (proof lines 9675-9683): by hypothesis every object admits a covering whose members map into one of the chosen objects, and on such members the map is bijective, as it is on their fibre products, so the sheaf condition gives bijectivity on the object itself.
proof_roadmap: Use the companion proposition on the localized sites and transport their points to the ambient site.
Reduce to showing that a map which is an isomorphism locally is an isomorphism.
Use the covering assumption and the sheaf condition to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for a site to have enough points: it suffices that the sheaves represented by a family of objects together surject onto the final object and that each localized site satisfies the hypotheses of the companion proposition (statement lines 9655-9666). The proof is a complete argument: the companion proposition gives enough points on each localized site and their points give points of the ambient site, so it suffices to show that a map of sheaves which is an isomorphism on every localized site is an isomorphism (proof lines 9668-9674); by hypothesis every object admits a covering whose members map into one of the chosen objects, and since the map is bijective on those members and on their fibre products, the sheaf condition gives bijectivity on the object (proof lines 9675-9683). The non-formal content is the reduction and the local-to-global step. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
